summary: An eon: 劫 renders kalpa by sound. The graph already meant to stop by force, and the eon’s end in fire lent it the sense of calamity.
placement: Chosen by farthest-point sampling on the integrated Lorenz-84 trajectory, so the eight stars spread across its projected shape. 望 takes the highest point, gazing up; 劫 the point farthest from the rest, at the edge of the eon. A design choice, not a claim.

satellites.title: An Eon, Borrowed by Sound
satellites.evidence: 劫 is short for 劫波, which renders kalpa by sound. In the Abhidharmakośa a great eon passes through formation, abiding, destruction and emptiness, and 所言成劫，謂從風起乃至地獄始有情生 — the eon of formation runs from the first wind to the first being born in hell.

checked.note: 所言成劫，謂從風起乃至地獄始有情生

satellites.title: A Graph That Meant Force
satellites.evidence: Before it meant an eon, 劫 meant to stop someone by force; the Shuowen: 人欲去，以力脅止曰劫. The translators chose a graph that already had a meaning, and the eon’s ending in fire later lent the word its sense of calamity, 劫難, 浩劫.
satellites.caveat: The Shuowen wording is from general knowledge; the route from kalpa to calamity is the usual explanation, not a documented step.
